draft.title: Repetition for effect
card: Repetition means using the same word, phrase or sentence pattern more than once. Writers do it on purpose.
Repeating something makes the reader notice it. Example: She was tired of waiting, tired of hoping, tired of being told to be patient. The word tired is stressed.
A repeated pattern creates a beat, a bit like a chorus in a song. This is why repetition can sound powerful when read aloud.
Repeated lines are easier to remember, so a passage with repetition can stay in the reader's mind.
draft.remember: Repetition stresses an idea, builds rhythm and helps a passage stick in the mind.

a.q: Which sentence uses repetition to stress an idea?
opts: We ran and ran and ran, until the field ended
We sprinted across the field and reached the old fence
Our legs burned as we crossed the wide, grassy field
The field was empty when we finally arrived there
a.why: The repeated word ran stresses how long and hard the speakers kept going. The other sentences describe the scene but do not repeat any word or pattern.
a.clue: Look for a word used again and again on purpose.

b.q: A speech says: We will not give up. We will not go quiet. We will not stand aside. What does the repeated pattern mainly do?
opts: Describes a setting for the reader
b.why: The repeated opening, We will not, makes a steady beat and stresses how strongly the speaker feels. It does not sound unsure, because repeating a firm phrase makes it sound more certain.
b.clue: Notice how each sentence begins the same way.

a.best: We ran and ran and ran, until the field ended
